<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

pij ships pod templates and type definitions as versioned originals. A pod command names a template by path or as `shipped:<name>[@v<n>]`; `adopt` and `init` copy them to governance or `--into <path>`; `template-diff` shows upstream changes and applies nothing. Nothing launches a seat.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- A repo owns its templates wherever it keeps them, and pij's shipped set improves for everyone.

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- Pulling upstream changes automatically.

| ac-0003 | `pij pod template-diff &lt;path&gt;` shows what changed upstream since the copy's version and applies nothing. | [ ] unchecked | — | — | [bp-0002](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | — |
| ac-0004 | `pij community init --seeds all --templates &lt;names&gt; [--into &lt;path&gt;] --why &lt;text&gt;` copies the ten type definitions into governance and the named templates into governance or the path, one commit per place, and prints what it wrote and where. | [ ] unchecked | — | — | [bp-0003](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | — |

## Risks

| risk | likelihood | impact | mitigation |

| A copy at a path in the main repo is edited by hand. | Medium | Low | That is its purpose: the repo owns its copy; diff still compares it with upstream. |

<a id="execution-guardrails"></a>

## Execution Guardrails

- Cost: one writer commit per adopt, init place or export; reads in-process; no seat launched; no loop, poll or timer.
- No permission rule changes (PRD 003); no daemon enforcement of a type's rules; no existing JSON field removed or renamed.
- Builds nice-19 through `just shared-build`, one at a time.
